questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: What is the principal legislation governing agrarian relations, tenancy, land ownership and land ceilings in Karnataka?

options.A: The Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964
options.B: The Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961
options.C: The Karnataka Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1957
options.D: The Karnataka Village Offices Abolition Act, 1961

questions.explanation: The Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961 (Karnataka Act No. 10 of 1962) is the principal state legislation governing agrarian relations, tenancy, land ownership and land ceilings in Karnataka.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: The Karnataka Land Reforms Act is numbered as which Karnataka Act?

options.A: Karnataka Act No. 10 of 1962
options.B: Karnataka Act No. 1 of 1974

questions.explanation: The Karnataka Land Reforms Act is Karnataka Act No. 10 of 1962.

questions.question: Why is the Act called the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961 although it is Act No. 10 of 1962?

options.A: Because it was amended in 1961
options.B: Because the Act is titled by the year in which it was framed; it was enacted and published as Karnataka Act 10 of 1962
options.D: Because the President assented to it in 1961

questions.explanation: The Act is titled by the year in which it was framed; it was enacted and published as Karnataka Act 10 of 1962.

questions.question: On which date was the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961 enacted as recorded by India Code?

options.B: 1 March 1974

questions.question: When did the Karnataka Land Reforms Act come into force?

options.A: 5 March 1962

questions.question: Under which Government Notification did the Karnataka Land Reforms Act come into force?

questions.question: To which territory does the Karnataka Land Reforms Act extend?

options.A: Only to the erstwhile Mysore State
options.B: To the whole State of Karnataka

questions.question: What was the broad purpose of enacting a uniform land-reform law for Karnataka?

options.A: To increase land revenue collection only
options.B: To establish uniform rules for agrarian relations, protect tenants, confer ownership on eligible cultivators, regulate agricultural holdings, impose ceilings and distribute surplus land
options.C: To abolish all private ownership of land

options.A: Krishna Committee
options.B: Jatti Committee

questions.question: What is the official name of the committee commonly called the Jatti Committee?

options.A: Mysore Tenancy and Agricultural Land Laws Committee

questions.question: When was the Jatti Committee constituted?

options.A: May 1957
options.B: March 1962

questions.explanation: The Mysore Tenancy and Agricultural Land Laws Committee (Jatti Committee) was constituted in May 1957.

questions.question: When did the Jatti Committee submit its recommendations?
questions.explanation: The Jatti Committee submitted its recommendations in 1961.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: What were the major weaknesses in Karnataka's pre-reform tenancy system?

options.A: Tenants had secure tenure and fair rents
options.B: Tenants often faced insecure tenure, high or unfair rents, risk of eviction, dependence on landlords and lack of ownership rights; tenancy rules also differed across regions
options.D: All tenants were already owners of their land

questions.explanation: Tenants often faced insecure tenure, high or unfair rents, risk of eviction, dependence on landlords and lack of ownership rights; tenancy rules also differed across the regions integrated into Mysore State.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: Which major amendment transformed the Karnataka land-reform framework in 1974?

options.A: The Karnataka Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 1973, enacted as Karnataka Act 1 of 1974
options.B: The Karnataka Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 1961

questions.explanation: The Karnataka Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 1973, enacted as Karnataka Act 1 of 1974, brought the major tenancy and ownership changes into operation from 1 March 1974.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: Why is 1 March 1974 important in Karnataka land-reform history?

options.A: It is the date the Act was enacted
options.B: It is the effective date of the major 1974 amendment under which tenant-held agricultural lands vested in the State Government and eligible tenants could be registered as occupants
options.C: It is the date the Act was repealed
options.D: It is the date the Jatti Committee was constituted

questions.explanation: 1 March 1974 is the effective date of the major 1974 amendment under which tenant-held agricultural lands, subject to statutory conditions and exceptions, vested in the State Government and eligible tenants could be registered as occupants.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: What is agricultural tenancy?

options.A: Ownership of agricultural land by the government
options.B: The legal relationship in which a landowner or landlord lets agricultural land to a tenant for cultivation in return for rent or other agreed consideration
options.C: The sale of agricultural land to a tenant
options.D: The acquisition of agricultural land by the government

questions.explanation: Agricultural tenancy is the legal relationship in which a landowner or landlord lets agricultural land to a tenant for cultivation in return for rent or other agreed consideration.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: What was the main objective of tenancy reforms in Karnataka?

options.A: To increase land revenue for the state
options.B: To protect actual cultivators from arbitrary eviction, regulate rent, provide security of tenure and ultimately confer ownership rights on eligible tenants

questions.explanation: The main objective was to protect actual cultivators from arbitrary eviction, regulate rent, provide security of tenure and ultimately confer ownership rights on eligible tenants.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: What is meant by security of tenure?

options.A: The right of the landlord to evict tenants at will
options.B: Legal protection that prevents a tenant from being removed from cultivated land except on grounds and through procedures permitted by law
options.C: The obligation of the tenant to pay rent in cash only
options.D: The right of the government to acquire tenant land

questions.explanation: Security of tenure means legal protection that prevents a tenant from being removed from cultivated land except on grounds and through procedures permitted by law.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: What did the 1961 Act initially seek to do for existing tenants?

options.A: Immediately transfer ownership to all tenants
options.B: Provide statutory protection against eviction, regulate rent and tenancy conditions, restrict certain transfers and subletting, and introduce limits on agricultural holdings

questions.explanation: The 1961 Act provided statutory protection against eviction, regulated rent and tenancy conditions, restricted certain transfers and subletting, and introduced limits on agricultural holdings.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: What major change did the 1974 amendment make to the landlord-tenant relationship?

options.A: It abolished all tenancy without compensation
options.B: It provided for vesting in the State Government of lands held by tenants immediately before the appointed date, subject to statutory exceptions, and enabled eligible tenants to become registered occupants
options.C: It restored full powers to landlords

questions.explanation: The 1974 amendment provided for vesting in the State Government of lands held by tenants immediately before the appointed date, subject to statutory exceptions, and enabled eligible tenants to become registered occupants.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: What does Section 44 of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act deal with?

options.A: Registration of occupants
options.B: Vesting in the State Government of lands held by or in the possession of tenants immediately before the relevant date, subject to the Act

questions.explanation: Section 44 deals with vesting in the State Government of lands held by or in the possession of tenants immediately before the relevant date, subject to the Act.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: What does Section 45 of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act provide?

options.A: Constitution of Land Tribunals
options.B: Eligible permanent, protected and other tenants, and qualifying sub-tenants, to be registered as occupants of the lands they cultivated personally, subject to the Act's conditions and ceiling limits

questions.explanation: Section 45 provides for eligible permanent, protected and other tenants, and qualifying sub-tenants, to be registered as occupants of the lands they cultivated personally, subject to the Act's conditions and ceiling limits.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: Who could claim registration as an occupant under the 1974 reform scheme?

options.A: Any person who paid rent to a landlord
options.B: A person who qualified as a permanent tenant, protected tenant or other tenant, or a qualifying lawful sub-tenant, and who personally cultivated the land before vesting
options.D: Any person owning more than ten units of land

questions.explanation: A person who qualified as a permanent tenant, protected tenant or other tenant, or a qualifying lawful sub-tenant, and who personally cultivated the land before vesting, could claim registration subject to statutory conditions.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: What is a protected tenant under the Karnataka Land Reforms Act?

options.A: A tenant who held and personally cultivated the land continuously for at least twelve years before the appointed day, with specified inclusions for certain former regional tenancy-law categories
options.B: A tenant who paid rent for at least five years
options.C: A tenant who owned the land
options.D: A tenant who cultivated land for at least three years

questions.explanation: In the statutory definition, a protected tenant generally refers to a tenant who held and personally cultivated the land continuously for at least twelve years before the appointed day, with specified inclusions for certain former regional tenancy-law categories.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: What is a deemed tenant?

options.A: A tenant with a written lease
options.B: A person whom the Act treats as a tenant by operation of law even if a conventional written lease is absent, provided the statutory conditions are satisfied
options.C: A tenant who pays rent in kind
options.D: A tenant who has been evicted

questions.explanation: A deemed tenant is a person whom the Act treats as a tenant by operation of law even if a conventional written lease is absent, provided the statutory conditions are satisfied.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: What is meant by personal cultivation under the Act?

options.A: Cultivation through hired labour only
options.B: Cultivation on one's own account through one's own labour, family labour, or hired labour under personal supervision, as defined by the Act

questions.explanation: Personal cultivation includes cultivation on one's own account through one's own labour, family labour, or hired labour under personal supervision, as defined by the Act.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: Did the 1974 reform automatically make every agricultural worker an owner?

options.A: Yes, all agricultural workers became owners
options.B: No. Ownership registration depended on qualifying tenancy status, personal cultivation, the land being covered by the Act, filing and adjudication requirements, and ceiling-related conditions
options.C: Yes, but only in certain districts
options.D: No, because the Act was never implemented

questions.explanation: Ownership registration depended on qualifying tenancy status, personal cultivation, the land being covered by the Act, filing and adjudication requirements, and ceiling-related conditions.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: What happened to the landlord's title in land vested under Section 44?

options.A: The landlord retained full title
options.B: The landlord's rights, title and interest in the vested land ceased and vested in the State Government, subject to the statutory scheme for payment of an amount
options.C: The landlord's title was transferred to the tenant directly
options.D: The landlord was allowed to sell the land

questions.explanation: The landlord's rights, title and interest in the vested land ceased and vested in the State Government, subject to the statutory scheme for payment of an amount.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: Did the former landlord receive nothing after vesting?

options.A: Yes, the landlord received nothing
options.B: No. The Act provided for an amount payable by the State Government to the former landowner and other persons whose interests were extinguished, according to the statutory formula
options.C: The landlord received the land back after five years
options.D: The landlord received only the standing crops

questions.explanation: The Act provided for an amount payable by the State Government to the former landowner and other persons whose interests were extinguished, according to the statutory formula.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: What is the significance of Section 48 of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act?

options.A: It provides for the constitution of Land Tribunals to deal with applications and questions relating to registration of occupants under the Act
options.B: It provides for the ceiling on land holdings
options.C: It provides for disposal of surplus land
options.D: It provides for the certificate of registration

questions.explanation: Section 48 provides for the constitution of Land Tribunals to deal with applications and questions relating to registration of occupants under the Act.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: What was the role of the Land Tribunal in the 1974 reforms?

options.A: It collected land revenue
options.B: It examined tenancy claims and evidence, determined eligibility for registration as an occupant, and passed orders under the Act

questions.explanation: The Land Tribunal examined tenancy claims and evidence, determined eligibility for registration as an occupant, and passed orders under the Act.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: Which authority commonly received applications for registration of occupancy rights under Section 48A?

options.A: The Land Tribunal
options.B: The Revenue Commissioner

questions.explanation: Applications were made to the Land Tribunal in the prescribed manner under Section 48A.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: What document evidences the grant of occupancy rights under the Act?

options.A: The certificate of registration issued under Section 55
options.B: The title deed issued under Section 63

questions.explanation: The certificate of registration issued under Section 55 is the statutory certificate evidencing registration as an occupant.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: What restriction applied to transfer of land obtained as an occupant?

options.A: Section 61 imposed restrictions on transfer of land of which a tenant had become a registered occupant; the applicable statutory period and exceptions must be read from the version of the law governing the transaction
options.B: There was no restriction on transfer

questions.explanation: Section 61 imposed restrictions on transfer of land of which a tenant had become a registered occupant; the applicable statutory period and exceptions must be read from the version of the law governing the transaction.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: What is the difference between a tenant and an occupant under the reform scheme?

options.A: A tenant cultivates land under a tenancy relationship; an occupant is a person registered under the Act with statutory occupancy/ownership rights after the vesting and adjudication process
options.B: A tenant owns the land; an occupant rents it

questions.explanation: A tenant cultivates land under a tenancy relationship; an occupant is a person registered under the Act with statutory occupancy/ownership rights after the vesting and adjudication process.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: What is the meaning of the land-to-the-tiller principle?

options.A: Ownership or secure proprietary rights should be transferred to the person who actually cultivates the land rather than remaining concentrated in an absentee landlord
options.B: Land should be owned by the government
options.C: Land should be owned by the highest bidder
options.D: Land should be owned only by landlords

questions.explanation: The land-to-the-tiller principle is the agrarian reform principle that ownership or secure proprietary rights should be transferred to the person who actually cultivates the land rather than remaining concentrated in an absentee landlord.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: Which reform in Karnataka is most closely associated with the slogan 'land to the tiller'?

options.A: The 1961 Act
options.B: The major 1974 amendment to the Karnataka Land Reforms Act

questions.explanation: The major 1974 amendment to the Karnataka Land Reforms Act is most closely associated with the land-to-the-tiller reform.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: How was the land-to-the-tiller principle implemented in Karnataka?

options.A: Tenant-held lands covered by Section 44 vested in the State Government, and eligible tenants who personally cultivated them could be registered as occupants under Section 45 after adjudication
options.B: All land was directly transferred to landlords
options.C: Tenants were given cash compensation instead of land
options.D: The government purchased land and sold it at market rates

questions.explanation: Tenant-held lands covered by Section 44 vested in the State Government, and eligible tenants who personally cultivated them could be registered as occupants under Section 45 after adjudication.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: Why was the land-to-the-tiller principle introduced?

options.A: To increase absentee landlordism
options.B: To reduce absentee landlordism, remove the separation between ownership and cultivation, improve tenure security and give cultivators a direct stake in agricultural production

questions.explanation: It sought to reduce absentee landlordism, remove the separation between ownership and cultivation, improve tenure security and give cultivators a direct stake in agricultural production.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: Did the land-to-the-tiller principle apply without limits to every tenant's entire holding?

options.A: Yes, it applied without any limits
options.B: No. Registration was subject to the Act's eligibility rules, exclusions, ceiling limits and other statutory conditions
options.C: Yes, but only for small holdings
options.D: No, because the principle was never implemented

questions.explanation: Registration was subject to the Act's eligibility rules, exclusions, ceiling limits and other statutory conditions.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: What was the significance of occupancy rights for tenant farmers?

options.A: Occupancy rights gave eligible tenant cultivators a more secure and direct legal interest in the land, reducing their dependence on former landlords
options.B: Occupancy rights allowed tenants to sell land immediately without restriction
options.C: Occupancy rights made tenants employees of the government
options.D: Occupancy rights had no legal significance

questions.explanation: Occupancy rights gave eligible tenant cultivators a more secure and direct legal interest in the land, reducing their dependence on former landlords.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: What is a land ceiling in agrarian legislation?

options.A: The minimum area of agricultural land that a person must hold
options.B: The maximum area of agricultural land that a person or family may hold under the law; land above the permitted limit is treated as surplus and can be vested in the State
options.C: The total area of government land
options.D: The area of land exempt from taxation

questions.explanation: A land ceiling is the maximum area of agricultural land that a person or family may hold under the law; land above the permitted limit is treated as surplus and can be vested in the State.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: Which section of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act deals with the ceiling on land holdings?

options.A: Section 44
options.B: Section 45

questions.explanation: Section 63 deals with the ceiling on land holdings.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: What was the principal objective of imposing an agricultural land ceiling?

options.A: To prevent excessive concentration of agricultural land, identify surplus holdings and make land available for redistribution to eligible landless and poorer sections
options.B: To increase the size of large estates

questions.explanation: The objective was to prevent excessive concentration of agricultural land, identify surplus holdings and make land available for redistribution to eligible landless and poorer sections.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: What was the ceiling area stated in Section 63(2) of the amended Act for an individual or a family?

options.A: Five units
options.B: Ten units

questions.explanation: The statutory text states ten units as the basic ceiling area.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: How could the ceiling increase for a family with more than five members under Section 63(2)?

options.A: One unit for every family member above five, subject to a maximum of fifteen units
options.B: Two units for every family member above five, subject to an overall maximum of twenty units
options.C: Five units for every family member above five, subject to a maximum of thirty units

questions.explanation: The provision added two units for every family member above five, subject to an overall maximum of twenty units.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: What is the maximum ceiling for a family under the proviso to Section 63(2)?

options.A: Ten units
options.B: Fifteen units

questions.explanation: The maximum ceiling for a family under the proviso to Section 63(2) is twenty units.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: What does the term 'unit' mean for calculating the land ceiling?

options.A: One acre of any type of land
options.B: A standard measure based on one acre of A-class land or an equivalent extent of other classes of land calculated using the soil-classification formula in Schedule I
options.D: The market value of one acre of land

questions.explanation: A unit is a standard measure based on one acre of A-class land or an equivalent extent of other classes of land calculated using the soil-classification formula in Schedule I; it is not simply one acre for every type of land.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: Why is it incorrect to convert ten units automatically into ten acres?

options.A: Because the Act uses a land-quality and classification-based unit system; different classes of land may require different physical acreages to equal one unit
options.B: Because one unit equals two acres
options.C: Because units are measured in hectares
options.D: Because ten units equals twenty acres

questions.explanation: The Act uses a land-quality and classification-based unit system; different classes of land may require different physical acreages to equal one unit.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: Were all categories of land necessarily counted identically for ceiling purposes?

options.A: Yes, all land was counted identically
options.B: No. The Act contained rules on classification, aggregation and specified exemptions; the applicable statutory provisions and schedules determine how land is counted

questions.explanation: The Act contained rules on classification, aggregation and specified exemptions; the applicable statutory provisions and schedules determine how land is counted.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: What does Section 64 of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act regulate?

options.A: Registration of occupants
options.B: Future acquisition of land where the acquisition would cause a person or family to exceed the ceiling area

questions.explanation: Section 64 deals with future acquisition of land where the acquisition would cause a person or family to exceed the ceiling area.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: What does Section 65 require when a holding exceeds the ceiling?

options.A: It requires the landholder to pay a fine
options.B: It provides for surplus land above the ceiling to be surrendered to the State Government, subject to the Act
options.C: It requires the landholder to sell the land to the highest bidder
options.D: It requires the landholder to distribute the land among family members

questions.explanation: Section 65 provides for surplus land above the ceiling to be surrendered to the State Government, subject to the Act.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: What is a declaration of holding under Section 66?

options.A: It is the prescribed statement of land held by a person or family, furnished to the competent authority so that the ceiling and any surplus area can be determined
options.B: It is the certificate of registration as an occupant
options.C: It is the order of the Land Tribunal
options.D: It is the notification of the government

questions.explanation: It is the prescribed statement of land held by a person or family, furnished to the competent authority so that the ceiling and any surplus area can be determined.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: What happens to land surrendered as surplus under the Act?

options.A: It remains with the landholder
options.B: After the statutory process, the land vests in the State Government and may be disposed of under the Act's provisions, including Section 77
options.C: It is sold to the highest bidder
options.D: It is returned to the original owner

questions.explanation: After the statutory process, the land vests in the State Government and may be disposed of under the Act's provisions, including Section 77.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: Could a landholder freely sell surplus land before the statutory surplus determination?

options.A: Yes, there was no restriction
options.B: No. Section 74 restricted alienation of a holding exceeding the ceiling until the required declaration and determination process was completed; a transfer made contrary to the provision could be void
options.C: Yes, but only with the permission of the Land Tribunal
options.D: No, because all land sales were banned

questions.explanation: Section 74 restricted alienation of a holding exceeding the ceiling until the required declaration and determination process was completed; a transfer made contrary to the provision could be void.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: What was the intended social purpose of the land ceiling?

options.A: To reduce concentration of landownership, promote a more equitable distribution of productive assets and strengthen the position of small cultivators and landless agricultural workers
options.B: To increase the wealth of large landowners

questions.explanation: It was intended to reduce concentration of landownership, promote a more equitable distribution of productive assets and strengthen the position of small cultivators and landless agricultural workers.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: What is surplus agricultural land?

options.A: Land held beyond the ceiling permitted by the Karnataka Land Reforms Act
options.B: Land that is not cultivated

questions.explanation: Surplus agricultural land is the extent of land held beyond the ceiling permitted by the Karnataka Land Reforms Act.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: Who receives priority in the disposal of surplus land under the reform policy?

options.A: Large landowners
options.B: Eligible landless persons and other specified disadvantaged or economically weaker categories, subject to the Act and rules

questions.explanation: The statutory scheme prioritises eligible landless persons and other specified disadvantaged or economically weaker categories, subject to the Act and rules.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: Which section provides for disposal of surplus land?

options.A: Section 44
options.B: Section 63

questions.explanation: Section 77 deals with disposal of surplus land vested in the State Government.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: What is the expected benefit of distributing surplus land to landless agricultural workers?

options.A: It can provide an independent productive asset, strengthen livelihood security, reduce dependence on wage labour and widen access to agricultural ownership
options.B: It increases their dependence on landlords

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the 1974 reform is INCORRECT?

options.A: Tenant-held lands covered by Section 44 vested in the State Government
options.B: Eligible tenants could be registered as occupants under Section 45
options.C: Every agricultural worker automatically became an owner
options.D: Registration was subject to eligibility rules, personal cultivation and ceiling limits

questions.explanation: The 1974 reform did not automatically make every agricultural worker an owner. Ownership registration depended on qualifying tenancy status, personal cultivation, the land being covered by the Act, filing and adjudication requirements, and ceiling-related conditions.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the land ceiling is INCORRECT?

options.A: The basic ceiling in Section 63(2) is ten units
options.B: Two additional units are allowed for each family member above five
options.C: The overall maximum ceiling for a family is twenty units
options.D: Ten units always equals exactly ten acres of any type of land

questions.explanation: It is incorrect to convert ten units automatically into ten acres because the Act uses a land-quality and classification-based unit system; different classes of land may require different physical acreages to equal one unit.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the land ceiling is INCORRECT?

options.A: All categories of land were necessarily counted identically for ceiling purposes
options.B: The Act contained rules on classification, aggregation and specified exemptions
options.C: The unit is based on one acre of A-class land or its equivalent in other classes
options.D: The ceiling aimed to prevent excessive concentration of agricultural land

questions.explanation: Not all categories of land were counted identically. The Act contained rules on classification, aggregation and specified exemptions; the applicable statutory provisions and schedules determine how land is counted.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a protected tenant is INCORRECT?

options.A: A protected tenant generally held and personally cultivated land continuously for at least twelve years before the appointed day
options.B: Specified inclusions apply for certain former regional tenancy-law categories
options.C: A protected tenant is automatically a registered occupant under Section 55 without any adjudication
options.D: Protected tenants were among those who could claim registration as occupants under Section 45

questions.explanation: A protected tenant was eligible to claim registration as an occupant subject to statutory conditions and adjudication; registration was not automatic without the Section 48A process and Section 55 certificate.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the land-to-the-tiller principle is INCORRECT?

options.A: It is the principle that ownership or secure proprietary rights should be transferred to the person who actually cultivates the land
options.B: It is most closely associated with the 1974 amendment
options.C: It applied without any limits to every tenant's entire holding
options.D: It sought to reduce absentee landlordism

questions.explanation: The principle did not apply without limits; registration was subject to the Act's eligibility rules, exclusions, ceiling limits and other statutory conditions.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.topic: Impact and Limitations of Land Reforms
questions.chapter: Impact and Limitations of Land Reforms
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the impact of Karnataka's land reforms is INCORRECT?

options.A: Eligible tenant cultivators gained the opportunity to obtain registered occupancy rights
options.B: Land reforms eliminated rural land inequality completely
options.C: Implementation was uneven and land inequality continued in many areas
options.D: Ownership rights can strengthen incentives to invest in land improvement

questions.explanation: Karnataka's land reforms did not eliminate rural land inequality completely. Implementation was uneven and land inequality, fragmented holdings, landlessness and disputes over title continued in many areas.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.topic: Later Legal Changes and Exam Cautions
questions.chapter: Later Legal Changes and Exam Cautions
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the 2020 amendment is INCORRECT?

options.A: It repealed Sections 79A, 79B and 79C
options.B: It repealed Section 63 (land ceiling)
options.C: Sections 79A-79C dealt with restrictions on acquisition and holding of agricultural land by specified persons
options.D: The repeal of Sections 79A-79C should not be confused with the land ceiling in Section 63

questions.explanation: The 2020 amendment did not repeal Section 63. Sections 79A-79C and Section 63 dealt with different legal matters; repeal of Sections 79A-79C did not mean that the land-ceiling provision itself was repealed.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: The Karnataka Land Reforms Act was enacted and published as which Act, although it is titled 1961?

options.A: Karnataka Act 10 of 1962
options.B: Karnataka Act 1 of 1974

questions.explanation: The Act is titled by the year in which it was framed; it was enacted and published as Karnataka Act 10 of 1962.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the scope of Section 44?

options.A: Vesting in the State Government of lands held by or in the possession of tenants immediately before the relevant date, subject to the Act
options.B: Registration of occupants

questions.explanation: Section 44 deals with vesting in the State Government of lands held by or in the possession of tenants immediately before the relevant date, subject to the Act.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the scope of Section 45?

options.A: Eligible permanent, protected and other tenants, and qualifying sub-tenants, to be registered as occupants of the lands they cultivated personally
options.B: Vesting of tenant-held lands in the State Government

questions.explanation: Section 45 provides for eligible permanent, protected and other tenants, and qualifying sub-tenants, to be registered as occupants of the lands they cultivated personally, subject to the Act's conditions and ceiling limits.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: Which of the following is a correct pairing of a section with its content?

options.A: Section 48A — applications and inquiry by the Tribunal
options.B: Section 48 — certificate of registration as occupant

questions.explanation: Section 48A deals with applications and inquiry by the Tribunal. Section 48 deals with Land Tribunals; Section 55 with the certificate of registration; Section 77 with disposal of surplus land.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: Which of the following is a correct pairing of a section with its content?

options.A: Section 64 — future acquisition exceeding the ceiling
options.B: Section 65 — ceiling on land holdings

questions.explanation: Section 64 deals with future acquisition of land where the acquisition would cause a person or family to exceed the ceiling area. Section 65 deals with surrender; Section 66 with declaration of holding; Section 74 with restriction on alienation.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: Which of the following is a correct pairing of a section with its content?

options.A: Section 63 — ceiling on land holdings
options.B: Section 64 — surrender of surplus land

questions.explanation: Section 63 deals with the ceiling on land holdings. Section 64 deals with future acquisition; Section 65 with surrender; Section 77 with disposal of surplus land.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: Which of the following correctly states the eligibility criteria for registration as an occupant under the 1974 scheme?

options.A: The person must have qualified as a permanent tenant, protected tenant or other tenant, or a qualifying lawful sub-tenant, and must have personally cultivated the land before vesting
options.B: The person must have owned at least ten units of land
options.C: The person must have been a landlord
options.D: The person must have paid rent in cash only

questions.explanation: A person who qualified as a permanent tenant, protected tenant or other tenant, or a qualifying lawful sub-tenant, and who personally cultivated the land before vesting, could claim registration subject to statutory conditions.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: Which of the following was NOT part of the 1961 Act's initial approach to tenancy?

options.A: Statutory protection against eviction
options.B: Regulation of rent and tenancy conditions
options.C: Restrictions on certain transfers and subletting
options.D: Immediate vesting of all tenant-held land in the State Government

questions.explanation: Immediate vesting of tenant-held land in the State Government came with the 1974 amendment (Section 44), not the 1961 Act. The 1961 Act provided protection against eviction, regulated rent and tenancy conditions, restricted certain transfers and subletting, and introduced limits on agricultural holdings.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.question: The land-to-the-tiller principle sought to reduce:

options.A: Absentee landlordism and the separation between ownership and cultivation
options.B: Tenure security
options.D: The stake of cultivators in agricultural production

questions.explanation: It sought to reduce absentee landlordism, remove the separation between ownership and cultivation, improve tenure security and give cultivators a direct stake in agricultural production.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.topic: Impact and Limitations of Land Reforms
questions.chapter: Impact and Limitations of Land Reforms
questions.question: Which of the following was a common implementation problem in land reforms?

options.A: Incomplete or inaccurate land records
options.B: Excessive speed of adjudication

questions.explanation: Problems included incomplete or inaccurate land records, disputes over actual cultivation, benami or concealed holdings, delays in adjudication, limited administrative capacity and difficulties in identifying eligible beneficiaries.

questions.subject: Karnataka Land Reforms
questions.topic: Impact and Limitations of Land Reforms
questions.chapter: Impact and Limitations of Land Reforms
questions.question: Why did some tenants fail to obtain occupancy rights despite the reform?

options.A: They could not establish qualifying tenancy or personal cultivation, missed procedural requirements, faced documentary gaps or disputes, or cultivated land falling within statutory exclusions
options.B: They refused to accept ownership
options.C: The Act did not allow tenants to apply

questions.explanation: Some could not establish qualifying tenancy or personal cultivation, missed procedural requirements, faced documentary gaps or disputes, or cultivated land falling within statutory exclusions.
